brief: The canvas displays a perpetual, amorphous vortex composed of hundreds of semi-transparent textual characters drawn from *Finnegans Wake*. These characters flow constantly and cyclically, forming a drifting, immersive stream across the surface. When the viewer clicks anywhere on the canvas, the surrounding characters are drawn toward the cursor, coalescing into a temporary, luminous cluster. This moment of concentration gives the text the stark, high-contrast appearance of old newsprint. Following this brief moment of clarity, the formed text does not instantly vanish, but instead undergoes a perceptibly gradual fade, dissolving smoothly back into the continuous, swirling background stream.

statement: This sketch creates an immersive, ever-shifting text vortex using characters from James Joyce's *Finnegans Wake*. Hundreds of semi-transparent letters flow in a continuous spiral, forming a hypnotic background stream. When clicked, the characters rush toward the center, creating a momentary burst of clarity and high-contrast density—like old newsprint suddenly focused. The effect is both organic and mechanical, with characters gradually fading back into the swirling chaos after the click. The visualization emphasizes the cyclical nature of language and meaning, where individual words gain prominence only briefly before dissolving back into the collective text.
